meta.project: Event Ops — Wedding Event Operations Platform

product_overview: Event Ops is a multi-tenant wedding event operations platform that centralizes guest management, RSVP calling, room allocation, and delivery proof capture for staff and clients. It replaces fragmented Excel, paper, and WhatsApp workflows with a single role-based system designed for mobile use and unreliable network conditions.
core_goals: Centralize wedding event operations in a single multi-tenant platform with strict event-level isolation
Support role-based access for admin, event_team, and client users with Postgres-enforced RLS
Provide reliable RSVP calling workflows with group locking, call logging, and review-before-commit extraction
Enforce room capacity and double-booking prevention at the database level
Capture tamper-evident delivery proofs with insert-only records and server-stamped timestamps
Make Excel imports idempotent so guest lists can be safely re-imported as they change
Expose read-only client views and operational dashboards while keeping base tables inaccessible to clients

features.name: Auth & Role Routing
features.description: Users log in and are routed to an appropriate experience based on their role, with access scoped to either all events, one event, or read-only client views.
user_flows: POST /api/auth/login with valid admin credentials -> Receive 200 with authenticated session/JWT -> GET role/profile data -> Receive admin routing context and full access

POST /api/auth/login with valid client credentials -> Receive 200 with authenticated session/JWT -> GET base table data -> Receive 200 with zero rows due to RLS -> GET client view data -> Receive read-only client road view
POST /api/auth/login with invalid credentials -> Receive 401 Unauthorized -> No session is created -> User remains on login screen

features.name: Multi-Tenancy & Fencing
features.description: Every record belongs to exactly one event, and row-level security plus composite foreign keys prevent cross-event access or references.
user_flows: GET event-scoped records with a valid event context -> Receive only rows for the current event -> POST a new child record with matching event_id -> Receive 201 Created with fenced data
POST a child record referencing a parent from another event -> Receive 400/403 or database constraint failure -> Cross-event reference is rejected -> No row is inserted
GET base tables without an allowed event membership -> Receive 200 with zero rows for client scope or denied access for unauthorized staff -> Other events remain hidden

features.name: RSVP Calling Operations
features.description: Staff can claim a group, place a call, log the outcome, capture audio, transcribe it, and review extracted fields before committing the RSVP update.
user_flows: GET /api/rsvp/queue -> Receive prioritized groups needing contact -> POST /api/rsvp/claim_group with a group id -> Receive 200 with exclusive lock -> POST /api/rsvp/call_attempts before dialing -> Receive 201 Created -> Use tel: deep link -> POST call outcome and audio metadata -> Receive queued sync state

POST /api/rsvp/claim_group for a group already locked by another device -> Receive 409 Conflict or lock failure -> Second caller cannot open the same group -> Queue remains locked until expiry or release

POST /api/rsvp/transcribe with uploaded audio -> Receive transcript result or retry behavior -> POST /api/rsvp/extract with transcript and current group context -> Receive strict JSON extraction -> POST /api/rsvp/review/commit after human edits -> Receive committed RSVP update
POST /api/rsvp/transcribe with corrupted or unsupported audio -> Receive error after retries -> Transcript status is marked failed -> UI surfaces failure instead of silently dropping the note

features.name: Room Assignment & Capacity
features.description: Admins can assign guest groups to hotel rooms while the system blocks over-capacity assignments and overlapping bookings.
user_flows: GET /api/rooms/hotels and /api/rooms/rooms -> Receive available hotel/room inventory -> POST /api/rooms/assignments with group, room, and dates -> Receive 201 Created if capacity and overlap checks pass -> GET room assignment chain -> Receive updated occupancy
POST /api/rooms/assignments with group PAX greater than room capacity -> Receive database guard failure or 400 response -> Assignment is rejected -> Room occupancy remains unchanged

POST /api/rooms/assignments that overlaps an existing booking for the same room -> Receive exclusion-constraint failure -> Double-booking is prevented at the database level -> No conflicting assignment is saved

features.name: Delivery Proofs
features.description: Staff can create delivery records and capture proof photos through the app, while the proof records remain immutable and server-stamped after insertion.
user_flows: POST /api/deliveries with deliverable details and in-app photo capture -> Receive 201 Created -> POST /api/delivery_proofs with queued image -> Receive 201 with server_recorded_at -> GET proof details -> Receive immutable proof record and signed access
POST /api/delivery_proofs with a gallery-selected image instead of in-app capture -> Receive validation failure -> Proof requirement is not satisfied -> Delivery remains unverified

PATCH /api/delivery_proofs/{id} or DELETE /api/delivery_proofs/{id} -> Receive 405/403 or database rule failure -> Proof cannot be altered or removed -> Only admin dispute fields, if supported, may change

features.name: Idempotent Import
features.description: Admins can import the source Excel repeatedly, previewing inserts/updates/skips before commit while preserving confirmed records and row-level hashes.
user_flows: POST /api/import/preview with an Excel file -> Receive preview of inserts, updates, and skips -> POST /api/import/commit after confirming mappings -> Receive 201 Created import batch -> GET import batch status -> Receive counts and operator metadata

POST /api/import/commit with the same file that was previously imported -> Receive 200/201 indicating no changes or only skipped rows -> Existing rows remain unchanged -> Idempotency is preserved via source-row hashes
POST /api/import/preview with malformed columns or missing required mappings -> Receive 400 validation error -> User must correct the column mapper -> No database writes occur
